    Module 0: Set up Rust and build Hello World

    By the end, you will be able to

    • Install the stable Rust toolchain with rustup.
    • Explain the jobs of rustup, rustc, and Cargo.
    • Build, run, format, check, and package a small application.

    Intuition

    Rust programs start at a function named main. The println! macro writes a line of text to the terminal. Rust checks the program before running it, so mistakes are reported early by the compiler.

    flowchart LR
  A[main function] --> B[println! macro]
  B --> C[Compiled binary]

    Install the toolchain

    The recommended installer is rustup. On Linux, macOS, or WSL, run:

    curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh

    Accept the default stable toolchain, then open a new terminal so the Cargo bin directory is on your PATH. On Windows, download and run rustup-init.exe from the official installation page. Windows builds may also need the Visual Studio C++ build tools.

    Verify the installation:

    rustup show
rustc --version
cargo --version

    Keep the stable toolchain current with rustup update. If a command is not found after installation, restart the terminal and check that $HOME/.cargo/bin is on PATH.

    The important commands

    Command Job
    rustup Installs and selects Rust toolchains and components.
    rustc Compiles a Rust source file directly.
    cargo Creates, builds, runs, tests, documents, and packages projects.
    rustfmt Formats Rust source consistently.
    clippy Finds common mistakes and non-idiomatic Rust.
    rustdoc Generates API documentation from Rust comments.
    rust-analyzer Gives editor features such as completion and diagnostics.

    The standard stable installation includes Cargo, rustfmt, and Clippy. If a component is missing, install it explicitly:

    rustup component add rustfmt clippy
rustup component add rust-src  # useful for rust-analyzer

    Most editors install or bundle rust-analyzer; VS Code uses the official extension. The compiler tools work independently of any editor.

    Create a Hello World application

    Cargo keeps the source layout and build metadata together. From the repository root, create a new application in a temporary directory:

    cargo new /tmp/hello-rust
cd /tmp/hello-rust

    Cargo creates Cargo.toml and src/main.rs. Replace src/main.rs with:

    fn main() {
    println!("Hello, Rust!");
}

    Build, run, and package it

    Run these commands inside /tmp/hello-rust:

    cargo check                 # type-check quickly without creating a binary
cargo build                 # debug build in target/debug/
cargo run                   # build if needed, then run the binary
cargo run -- Rust           # pass Rust as an argument to the binary
cargo build --release       # optimized build in target/release/
cargo test                  # run tests, when the project has tests
cargo doc --open            # build and open local API documentation
cargo package --allow-dirty # validate the package archive locally

    For this application, the release binary is target/release/hello-rust on Linux and macOS, or target/release/hello-rust.exe on Windows. cargo package creates a crate archive for distribution and checks that the package can be published. It does not upload anything. Use cargo publish only when you intend to publish a crate to crates.io.

    Format and lint before sharing

    cargo fmt                 # format the whole project
cargo fmt -- --check      # fail if formatting would change files
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

    rustfmt handles layout. Clippy provides advice about correctness, performance, and idiomatic style. Treat warnings as errors in CI when the project is ready for that policy.

    The commands above are the standard Rust workflow: check, format, lint, test, build, then create a release artifact.

    Run the course example

    The repository also contains a Cargo version of Hello World:

    cargo run --manifest-path examples/00-first-lesson/hello-world/Cargo.toml

    Expected output:

    Hello, Rust!

    Exercise

    Change the message in examples/00-first-lesson/hello-world/src/main.rs, run cargo fmt, and use cargo run --manifest-path examples/00-first-lesson/hello-world/Cargo.toml to see the result.

    Review

    1. Which command manages Rust toolchains?
    2. Which command runs the current Cargo package?
    3. Which command formats Rust source code?
